name: Sunday Night Impact (4/4/99)

date.source: The promotion's own seven-part broadcast posting, headed "Sunday Night Impact ... April 4, 1999."

matches.stipulation: GSWP World Heavyweight Championship tournament, first round
matches.note: Alex Cote won by submission with a dragon sleeper/surfboard combination after a back-and-forth outside brawl.

matches.stipulation: GSWP World Heavyweight Championship tournament, first round
matches.note: Eddie Rue won a controversial roll-up after Mike Wilson's own valet was knocked unconscious on the apron and Wilson's attempted ambush was countered.

matches.stipulation: GSWP World Heavyweight Championship tournament, first round
matches.note: Shawn Sylkk won by pinfall, then was attacked after the bell by Robbie Kincade over an unrelated grievance.

Brian Bradley won with a superplex through a table on the boardwalk outside the arena, after the brawl left the ring and the locker room area; Bradley continued the beatdown after the bell until two other wrestlers ran in.

no_appearances_reason: A scheduled tournament bout between "Regulator" Trent King and Tyrone Parker never started: Robbie Kincade, Fang, and King all walked out together and declared they would not fight one another, forming an informal alliance; Tyrone Parker is not otherwise shown on this broadcast and is not structured here.
notes: The promotion's own debut broadcast in this record, opening a seven-man single-elimination tournament for the then-vacant World Heavyweight Championship. Nathan Starr no-showed his own tournament bout and Shawn Parker advanced by forfeit; a fourth tournament match was called off when its participants refused to fight.

name: Sunday Night Impact (5/2/99)

date.source: The promotion's own six-part broadcast posting, headed "Sunday Night Impact ... May 2, 1999."

matches.note: Boltz won the title from "True Playa" Mike Wilson.

matches.stipulation: GSWP World Heavyweight Championship, main event
matches.note: Fang retained the title over Shawn Sylkk.

no_appearances_reason: Not served as a document; structured from the promotion's own broadcast for title-lineage continuity only. Johnny Glamour's own debut win over an unminted, one-off comedic opponent is not structured as a match; he is recorded here as an angle appearance for his debut.
notes: Not served as a document, per no-bulk-mirroring; read for title-lineage continuity. On this broadcast the promotion's own owner, Marcus Robinson, also announced a new Extreme Championship, to be decided the following week by a three-way match among Derek Douglas, Robbie Kincade, and a third wrestler not otherwise structured in this record; that match itself does not survive in this record, and Derek Douglas is billed as the champion by the promotion's own next surviving broadcast.

name: Sunday Night Impact (5/30/99)

date.source: The promotion's own seven-part broadcast posting, headed with a countdown to the promotion's own summer Pay-Per-View "two weeks away."

matches.note: Boltz won a non-title contenders match over the promotion's own former Television Champion; Boltz does not appear among the four entrants in the title match at the promotion's own following Pay-Per-View, and the read record does not explain why.

"Ice Storm" Chris Winters, already billed as the reigning Television Champion, won a non-title match; Adam Morley helped him fight off the three Television title contenders who confronted him afterward.
Fang, already billed as the reigning World Heavyweight Champion, won a non-title main event over "Heartless" Eddie Rue.

no_appearances_reason: Not served as a document; structured from the promotion's own broadcast for title-lineage continuity only. Two further matches (an opening bout and a hardcore-styled tag feud preview) involve wrestlers not otherwise structured in this record and are not included here.
notes: Not served as a document, per no-bulk-mirroring; read for title-lineage continuity. Boltz returned from an apparent absence to attack the promotion's own former Television Champion and demand a rematch he felt he was owed. In a separate hardcore-styled non-title match, Robbie Kincade was seriously injured off a table spot against Hardcore Carey; he is not shown again in this record.

name: 1999 Summer Showdown

date.source: The promotion's own fourteen-part Pay-Per-View posting, which frames the show as live from a sold-out Manhattan Center on "June 13, 1999."

matches.note: Adam Morley won by pinfall with a springboard rocker dropper.
TJ Masters won a hardcore-styled brawl that spilled to the outside and through a ringside table.
Dylan Ryder won by pinfall after a stalling promo by his opponent, who refused to wrestle before eventually being pinned.

matches.stipulation: Hardcore, number-one contender's match for the GSWP Extreme Championship
matches.note: Adrian Trust won with a flamethrower slam through a burning table, earning a future Extreme title shot.

matches.title: gswp-1999-extreme
matches.note: "Double D" Derek Douglas retained the GSWP Extreme Championship.

Eddie Rue won by disqualification after a masked man interfered; the masked man struck Rue rather than Williams, and the referee ruled against Williams regardless. The masked man was unmasked afterward as "Hate Child" Ethan Love, revealed to be Rue's own secret partner all along.

matches.title: gswp-1999-television
matches.note: "Ice Storm" Chris Winters retained the GSWP Television Championship, pinning Tha Dragon with a Freezer Burn in the match's final fall after Christian Madison and Mike Wilson were eliminated earlier in the contest.

matches.title: gswp-1999-world-heavyweight
matches.note: Johnny Glamour won the GSWP World Heavyweight Championship after King Snake, a returning veteran aligned with Glamour, struck the champion with a chair; a fourth wrestler's run-in to help Fang arrived too late. Glamour and King Snake declared themselves in charge of the promotion afterward.

notes: The promotion's own summer Pay-Per-View, its most extensive surviving broadcast in this record: two title defenses, a new World Heavyweight Champion, and a surprise appearance by a veteran crossover star. A battle royal for a new midcard "Garden State" title, announced here for two weeks later, is not in the read record.

name: "Ice Storm" vs. James Sandison (7/11/99)

date.source: The promotion's own posting, dated 11 July 1999.

matches.title: gswp-1999-television
matches.note: "Ice Storm" Chris Winters retained the GSWP Television Championship in a grueling defense.

notes: A single title defense rather than a full broadcast. Immediately after the match, TJ Masters ambushed Sandison to settle an unrelated score, and "Magnificent" Mike Douglas then attacked the champion with a chair, framing it as a message to fellow wrestler Adam Morley; Adam Morley and Shawn Sylkk ran in to help Winters.

name: "Deathwish" Jonathan Christopher vs. Terrance Goldsworthy

date.source: The match states no date of its own; its only surviving copy was reposted on 1 September 2001 as a writing sample.

matches.note: A rematch from the promotion's last pay-per-view, one fall with a 15-minute limit. Goldsworthy wins with a top-rope powerbomb after an earlier three count was waved off for his foot on the rope.

notes: A single match rather than a full broadcast, called by Rick Fuller and Johnny Martoni and announced by Mike Capone; the commentary names Duke Putrid as the reigning World Champion.
